questions.q: What is the only contact patch between the car and the road?
questions.explain: All grip, braking and steering pass through the four small contact patches of the tyres — there is no other direct contact between the car and the road.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a winter tyre over a summer tyre?
options: Its rubber stays flexible and grips better in cold, snow and ice
It’s especially suited to driving in intense heat
It doesn’t need a pressure check
questions.explain: A winter tyre is made from a softer rubber compound and a tread pattern that stays effective in cold, snow and ice — far more than a summer tyre.

questions.q: What is true about a run-flat tyre after all the air has left it?
options: It allows a short, slow continuation to a garage, and afterward it must be replaced — not repaired
You must not drive on it even one metre
questions.explain: The reinforced sidewall of a run-flat tyre carries the car even without air, for a short distance and at limited speed only — and then it must be replaced.

questions.q: In the code 205/55R16 on the tyre sidewall, what does the number 205 refer to?
options: The sidewall height-to-width ratio as a percentage
The wheel rim diameter in inches
questions.explain: 205 is the tyre’s width in millimetres; 55 is the sidewall height-to-width ratio; R is radial construction; 16 is the rim diameter in inches.

questions.q: What does the speed rating (the letter) that appears after the rim size indicate?
options: The maximum speed the tyre is designed to carry safely
questions.explain: The speed rating, for example V, indicates the maximum speed the tyre is designed to carry safely at full load.

questions.q: The code 2324 inside an oval on the tyre sidewall indicates —
questions.explain: The first two digits are the week of manufacture and the last two are the year: 2324 = week 23 of 2024.

questions.q: Up to how many years from the manufacturing date may a tyre repair shop fit a new tyre on a car?
options: There is no such limit in law
questions.explain: Regulation 322(b1): a tyre must not be fitted if more than {{fact:tyre.max_age_fit_new}} have passed since its manufacture date, or {{fact:tyre.max_age_fit_used}} if it is used.

questions.q: Where is the correct tyre pressure for the car shown?
options: Every driver decides based on feel
On the vehicle manufacturer’s sticker, usually in the driver’s door opening
questions.explain: The vehicle manufacturer — not the tyre manufacturer — sets the correct tyre pressure, and shows it on a sticker in the door opening or on the fuel cap.

questions.q: When is the right time to check tyre pressure?
options: When the tyres are cold — before driving or after a very short drive
Only once a year, before the annual inspection
Right after a long drive, when the tyres are hot
There’s no difference between a hot and a cold tyre
questions.explain: Hot air expands and raises the measured pressure; checking when the tyre is cold gives the true value.

questions.q: What does tyre pressure that’s too low cause?
options: Wear in the centre of the tread only
Wear at both edges of the tread, overheating and higher fuel consumption
questions.explain: At low pressure the tyre bulges inward, wears at the edges, heats up and increases fuel consumption.

questions.q: What is the role of the TPMS system?
options: Warn when the pressure in one of the wheels drops below the required level
Completely prevent a tyre blowout in every situation
questions.explain: TPMS monitors pressure in every wheel and lights a warning when it drops — but it doesn’t replace a regular manual check.

questions.q: What is the minimum tread depth allowed on a pneumatic tyre, including the spare wheel?
options: There is no minimum value in law
questions.explain: Regulation 322(c): the tread depth must not be less than {{fact:tyre.min_tread}}, including on the spare wheel.

questions.q: What is the role of the wear indicators inside the tyre’s grooves?
options: Mark the minimum tread depth allowed — when the tread wears level with them, the tyre fails
questions.explain: The wear indicators are small raised bars at the bottom of the grooves, at the height of the minimum depth allowed by law.

questions.q: A tyre is worn mainly in the centre of the tread, with both edges in relatively good condition. What’s the likely reason?
questions.explain: Pressure that’s too high bulges the tyre outward, so most of the contact and wear concentrates in the centre of the tread.

questions.q: Especially worn tread mainly increases the risk of —
questions.explain: Worn tread can’t clear water fast enough, and the tyre loses contact with the wet road.

questions.q: A puncture happens on a non-urban road. What’s the correct first step?
options: Get out immediately and start changing the wheel on the shoulder
Keep driving to a petrol station, even if it’s far away
Call the police before doing anything else
Stop somewhere safe, well clear of the traffic, turn on the hazard lights and put on a hi-vis vest before getting out
questions.explain: Safety comes first: a safe spot, hazard lights and a hi-vis vest before you get out of the car and start working.

questions.q: From what distance must the warning triangle be visible to a driver approaching from behind, when the car has had to stop on the road?
options: There is no distance requirement in law
questions.explain: Regulation 70(a): the warning triangle must be placed so it can be seen from at least {{fact:equip.triangle.visibility}} away.

questions.q: Where do you place the jack when changing a wheel?
options: At any flat point under the car
Only at the lifting point the vehicle manufacturer set on the chassis
Under the centre of the gearbox
questions.explain: Only the lifting points the vehicle manufacturer set are strong enough to carry the car’s weight on the jack; another spot could break or slip.

questions.q: What is true about a space-saver spare (“skinny spare”)?
options: It’s meant for permanent use instead of a regular tyre
You may drive on it without limit, exactly like a regular wheel
It’s meant only to get you to the nearest garage, at limited speed and distance
questions.explain: A space-saver spare is smaller and narrower than the regular tyres, and is meant only to get you to the nearest garage — at limited speed and distance.

questions.q: What is the purpose of tyre rotation?
options: To swap the front tyres with the rear ones so they wear evenly
To balance weight inside the wheel
questions.explain: The front tyres usually carry more steering and braking load and wear faster; rotation balances this out.

questions.q: Vibration in the steering wheel that’s felt at a certain speed and disappears at another speed usually indicates —
questions.explain: An unbalanced wheel causes vibration felt mainly in a certain speed range, because of uneven weight distribution in the wheel.

questions.q: What does the law state about tyres fitted on the same axle?
options: There is no requirement in law
You may combine radial and diagonal on the same axle
They must be identical in size, load capacity and construction (radial or diagonal)
You may combine different sizes if they look similar
questions.explain: Regulation 322(d)(1): tyres that differ in size, load capacity or construction must not be fitted on the same axle.
